PASS only for the scoped A–F sufficient-family result, relative to the task’s explicitly imported foundations. This establishes a countable divisorial criterion on P² and the stated genuinely nonclosed example. It does not complete original P06, classify general ideal positivity, settle an unrestricted zero-volume implication, or establish a modification mass law.

I independently checked the supplied current author proof, the complete original review, and all five complete independent notes. Their support DAG is n1: []; n2: [n1]; n3: [n1,n2]; n4: [n1,n2,n3]; n5: [n1,n2,n3,n4]. Earlier verdicts, root assessments, hashes, execution records and algebra-test claims were not correctness grants. The historical INCONCLUSIVE remains a record of that assessment; the later authentication failure supplies no mathematical verdict.

All nonroutine foundational theorems used here are explicitly imported by the current task, including foundations 15–16. No additional nonroutine external premise is needed. Accordingly premises and passages are empty. This is a proof relative to the permitted background, not a claim of self-contained or recursive certification of those foundations. I opened matching primary sources and checked the applications below.

A. Normalize each defining section to have unit coefficient norm. Then ℓ_j≤0. Unitary invariance of the standard Fubini–Study probability measure gives the density 2(1−x) for x=|s_j(Z)|²/||Z||². Consequently ∫ℓ_jκ²=−3/2, and Tonelli gives ∫|u₀|κ²=3A/2. The finite partial sums decrease in a common Aκ background, so their pointwise limit is genuine and is not identically −∞. Its supremum is finite. Poincaré–Lelong gives dd^c u=S−Aκ, where S=Σa_j[H_j] is a finite-mass closed positive current. Hence θ+dd^c u=R+S≥R>0. This proves strict admissibility and bigness directly, without assuming a volume conclusion. The normalization agrees with [Demailly’s Poincaré–Lelong formulas](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~demarco/Math274/Demailly_ComplexAnalyticDiffGeom.pdf), III.2.15 and V.13.2.

Fix any specified compact smooth modification π:Z→P² and any prime E. For the tail r_K=Σ_{j>K}a_jℓ_j, write A_K=Σ_{j>K}a_j. Its canonical pullback is genuine: local smooth corrections make it psh, and it is finite somewhere on the biholomorphic locus. Thus T_K=A_Kπ*κ+dd^c(r_K∘π) is closed and positive. [Gauduchon’s Theorem 2](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf) supplies a smooth η>0 with dd^cη=0 on this compact surface. The even-Betti hypothesis belongs to Theorem 1 and is not needed. Closed divisorial subtraction and distributional Stokes give
ν_E(r_K∘π)∫_Eη≤∫_Z T_K∧η=A_K∫_Zπ*κ∧η.
The denominator is strictly positive. Therefore ν_E(r_K∘π)≤C_EA_K→0. Finite additivity now gives
ν_E(u∘π)=Σ_{j≤K}a_j ord_E(π*H_j)+ν_E(r_K∘π),
which proves both convergence and the exact asserted b(E). Constants may depend on the fixed modification and divisor; uniformity over all modifications is unnecessary. No restriction of u to E is assumed.

The independent n1 tail proof also works. On each pullback coordinate chart, normalized sections form a compact family of holomorphic combinations with no identically zero member. Convergent coefficients yield a nonzero limiting holomorphic function. A point outside its zero set, submean inequalities and overlapping coordinate balls provide local L¹ bounds for the logarithms. Foundation 15 then provides subsequential L¹ compactness; convergence outside the limiting zero set identifies the limit. Compactness of the coefficient sphere and a finite chart cover yield a uniform global pullback L¹ bound. Thus ||r_K∘π||₁=O(A_K). Integration against an arbitrary Hermitian h_Z correctly retains the term ∫(r_K∘π)dd^c h_Z and bounds the tail trace by O(A_K). Local Lelong trace estimates give the claimed tail bound. The descending valuation filtration of the finite-dimensional space of linear sections also terminates, since a nonzero pulled-back section cannot vanish to infinite generic order.

BMP is established independently. Given any Hermitian h, choose Cκ≥h. For bounded genuine h-psh f, bounded-product positivity and multilinearity give
0≤(h+dd^c f)²≤(Cκ+dd^c f)².
The right-hand product has total mass C² by the global bounded Bedford–Taylor recursion and Stokes. In particular v₊(κ)=1. This is an upper-mass assertion; no positive lower singularity volume is inferred from BMP.

B. Choose a sufficiently large integer C with Cκ≥θ. Both u and v belong to the same closed positive Cκ background on Kähler P². The hypothesis includes every smooth projective modification and every further point blowup. The generic coefficient of the exceptional divisor recovers the point Lelong number. Therefore the exact hypotheses of [Darvas–Xia Theorem 2.13 and Proposition 2.30](https://research.chalmers.se/publication/528300/file/528300_Fulltext.pdf) are satisfied. Their growth normalization uses log||z||, giving twice the present log-squared divisor coefficients; equality is unaffected. Their ideals use exp(−tφ). Nothing identifies the nonclosed θ with a line-bundle curvature.

The converse on every arbitrary compact modification follows from the independently reconstructed local estimate. For a local quasi-psh φ, put b=ν_E(φ∘π), e_k=ord_E(I(kφ)O_Z), and j_E=ord_E(Jac π). Smooth additions make φ psh without changing its ideals or coefficients. Near a generic smooth point of E, closed subtraction gives φ∘π≤b log|ζ₁|²+O(1). Pullback integrability, retaining the Jacobian, forces
ord_E(g∘π)+j_E+1>kb
for every germ g in I(kφ). This gives e_k/k≥b−(j_E+1)/k.

[Demailly’s local Bergman Theorem 1.2 and Lemma 1.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.5432v2) allow every real m>0. Taking m=k/2 gives φ_m=k⁻¹logΣ|g_{m,ℓ}|²≥φ−O(1/k). The terms belong to I(kφ); finite extraction gives their subideal J_k and its generic order. Crucially, J_k⊆I(kφ), so
 e_k/k≤ord_E(J_kO_Z)/k=ν_E(φ_m∘π)≤b.
No identification of this subideal with the whole multiplier ideal is required. Hence e_k/k→b. Equality of actual ideals at integer weights therefore implies equality of coefficients on every given modification. Together with the projective-modification theorem, this proves B for every positive real weight.

[BFJ Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487) originally concerns stabilized J₊ ideals and exp(−2tφ). [Guan–Zhou strong openness](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n2-p05-p.pdf) identifies those stabilized ideals with actual ideals; replacing the weight parameter by t/2 supplies the present convention. Its local negative-polydisc hypotheses are met after shrinking, adding a smooth correction and subtracting a constant. Darvas–Xia Proposition 2.14’s unconverted numerical formula is excluded. For example, φ=c log|z₁|² has growth-normalized Lelong number 2c, while k⁻¹ord I(kφ) tends to c. The equality theorem and the correctly normalized estimate above survive this discrepancy.

C. The normalized u is an ideal-equivalent competitor, so the envelope does not collapse. Finite maxima preserve the full modification profile. For a fixed divisor this follows by subtracting the common divisorial logarithm: the maximum retains a coefficient at least b, while domination of either input gives the opposite inequality. Maximum stability in the nonclosed θ background follows locally from smooth convex maximum approximations with a common arbitrarily small smooth error, followed by distributional passage to the limit.

Include u in every finite maximum of a Choquet sequence. The resulting genuine competitors f_j increase, satisfy u≤f_j≤0, and converge almost everywhere to q. A common closed local correction supplies the genuine usc envelope; weak convergence retains θ+dd^c q≥0. For each fixed modification, the pullbacks converge locally in L¹, dominated by the genuine pullback of u. Positivity after subtracting b(E)[E] persists under the weak-current limit, giving ν_E(q∘π)≥b(E). Equivalently one may use point Lelong upper semicontinuity at a point outside the countably many nongeneric loci. Since q≥u, the reverse inequality holds. Thus the entire profile survives the envelope before any mass or ordinary-type assumption.

Siu subtraction from Cκ+dd^c q removes every finite partial sum of S; the increasing divisorial limit remains subtractable. Hence
(C−A)κ+dd^c(q−u)≥0.
The difference is first taken in L¹ and then represented canonically. Its quasi-psh representative is bounded above on compact P². Canonical uniqueness identifies q with u plus this representative everywhere, including common poles. Thus q≤u+constant; together with q≥u this proves q∼u.

The independent n2 route is valid as well. For a competitor ζ, subtract S only from its closed auxiliary current. To prove positivity of θ+dd^cζ−S, split measure coefficients on P=⋃H_j and its complement: the smooth correction has zero restriction to P, while outside P the remaining current equals the original positive current. This works even when the complement of the countable union is not open. The canonical residual ψ=ζ−u₀ is consequently R-psh. All such residuals belong to a fixed closed Bκ background. [Guedj–Zeriahi Proposition 1.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0401302), applied to ψ/2 because its dd^c is twice the present operator, bounds sup ψ by its smooth-volume mean plus one uniform constant. The obstacle bound ζ≤0 bounds that mean. Therefore all competitors satisfy ζ≤u₀+constant uniformly, and u sandwiches the envelope from below.

The same proof works for each smooth obstacle F, using a constant c with u+c≤F. For an ordinary competitor η≤F with η≼u, max(η,u+c) is below F and ordinarily equivalent to u, hence is an ideal-equivalent competitor. Conversely the ideal envelope is ordinarily equivalent to u and is an ordinary competitor. This proves ordinary/ideal equality at every smooth obstacle for the constructed u. It does not assert the same ordinary-envelope conclusion for every starting v having only its ideal profile. This envelope mechanism is already known countable divisorial background and retains that credit.

D. Let w be ANY genuine θ-psh potential ordinarily equivalent to q. By C, w∼u. It has the prescribed base divisor coefficients. Closed subtraction gives
T=Cκ+dd^c w=S+K,  K=(C−A)κ+dd^c h≥0,
where h is the canonical representative of the L¹ difference w−u. Ordinary equivalence bounds h almost everywhere. Canonical local averaging extends both bounds everywhere. Thus h is globally bounded; no pointwise subtraction of infinities has been used.

K has bounded local psh potentials. [Bedford–Taylor bounded-product and capacity theory](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf) implies that its trace charges no pluripolar set. S is supported on actual poles of w, whereas K ignores the entire pole set. The degree-one non-pluripolar current is therefore exactly K, including when there are additional poles beyond the named divisor union. For every smooth dd^c-closed form ρ, distributional Stokes gives
∫ρ∧K=(C−A)∫ρ∧κ.

The author’s closed top-mass argument is correct. Finite logarithmic sums u_N have actual closed mass (C−A_N)². In the fixed closed Cκ background, monotonicity compares u to u_N and gives the upper bound. Positive closed non-pluripolar multilinearity gives the lower bound (C−A)². Letting N increase gives equality. Applying closed monotonicity in both ordinary-order directions then yields ∫⟨T²⟩=(C−A)² for every w∼u. All these currents are closed on Kähler P²; the relevant hypotheses are those of [BEGZ Propositions 1.4 and 1.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674) and [Witt Nyström’s monotonicity theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1). Neither theorem is applied to θ.

The independent n3 proof establishes the stronger measure identity ⟨T²⟩=K². Put S_N=T−Σ_{j≤N}a_j[H_j]. These currents remain closed positive and have class (C−A_N)[κ]. Removing finitely many divisors leaves the non-pluripolar square unchanged, because the currents agree on the open complement of that finite union and both products ignore the union. Bounded truncations of a genuine global potential for S_N give the mass bound ∫⟨T²⟩≤(C−A_N)². Positive multilinearity gives ⟨T²⟩≥K², and bounded Stokes gives ∫K²=(C−A)². The positive difference has zero total mass as N→∞. This argument assumes no open complement of the whole countable divisor union.

Put L=Cκ−θ. Use the SAME w_j=max(w,−j) in both backgrounds, restricted to the SAME strict sets {w>−j}. Bounded multilinearity gives
1_{w>−j}(θ+dd^c w_j)²
=1_{w>−j}(Cκ+dd^c w_j)²−2L∧1_{w>−j}(Cκ+dd^c w_j)+1_{w>−j}L².
The closed degree-two restrictions increase to a finite product. The degree-one restrictions increase with finite trace to K. Smooth multiplication preserves these finite correction limits, and L² ignores poles. Hence the actual finite measure identity is
MA_ext,θ(w)=⟨T²⟩−2L∧K+L².
This uses [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu’s bounded construction, Section 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090); the unbounded exhaustion has been justified explicitly, rather than inferred from a blanket nonclosed theorem.

Because dd^cθ=0, also dd^cL=0. Integration therefore gives
∫MA_ext,θ(w)=(C−A)²−2(C−A)∫L∧κ+∫L²=∫(θ−Aκ)²>0.
This proves the formula for the entire ordinary type. Its infimum and supremum consequently equal the displayed number. The independent residual calculation agrees: the corrected measure is (R+dd^c h)², and both ∫R∧dd^c h and ∫(dd^c h)² vanish by dd^cR=0 and the global bounded recursion. Omitting pluriclosedness would leave a residual-dependent term. No assertion is made for every merely ideal-equivalent potential, whose residual can be unbounded.

E. Compact support of the real cutoff makes α and τ smooth after extension. The two summands defining τ are conjugate, so τ is real of type (1,1). The identities ∂²=bar∂²=0 imply ∂bar∂τ=0 globally, including the cutoff region. Where χ=1,
τ=bar z₂ dz₂∧dbar z₁−z₂ dz₁∧dbar z₂,
dτ=dz₂∧dbar z₂∧(dz₁−dbar z₁)≠0.
If C_τ is the maximum κ-operator norm of τ, any ε>0 with εC_τ≤1/2 gives θ≥κ/2. Thus θ is positive and pluriclosed but genuinely nonclosed. With A=1/4, R≥κ/4, so ∫R²≥1/16.

The normalized vectors [1:t_j:t_j²] are distinct, and their three-by-three determinants are nonzero Vandermonde determinants. Therefore no three corresponding lines belong to one pencil. Each H_j has coefficient a_j>0. An analytic singularity type on a compact base has only finitely many positive prime divisorial components, by local finite generation and a finite relatively compact chart cover. The local actual-ideal order limit from B applies to any quasi-psh analytic representative and would force infinitely many such components if its weighted ideals agreed with those of u. This excludes an analytic ideal type, while individual multiplier ideals remain coherent.

The additional n4 torsion calculation also checks out. Set η=∂α. Since d(α+barα)=τ+η+barη, surface bidegrees and Stokes give ∫κ∧τ=0 and ∫τ²=−2∫η∧barη. The latter integral is strictly positive before multiplication by −2, since η is nonzero on an open subset. Hence the common mass is 9/16−2ε²∫η∧barη, rather than the closed-background polynomial 9/16. Pointwise residual positivity supplies the asserted lower bound. The manifold is projective; no non-Kähler manifold is claimed.

F. For smooth real f, w↦w−f is an invertible transport between the specified ordinary types in θ and θ+dd^c f. It preserves genuine representatives, canonical poles and actual currents. At every weight exp(−t(w−f))=exp(tf)exp(−tw), and the smooth factor is locally bounded above and below by positive constants, so every multiplier ideal is unchanged. Transport a sufficiently large closed auxiliary background Ω to Ω+dd^c f. The auxiliary current and the smooth difference Ω−θ remain unchanged, so the corrected measure is identical. The entire-type bijection therefore preserves both extremal volumes.

Competitors and obstacles transport exactly, giving
P_(θ+dd^c f,F−f)[v−f]_I=P_(θ,F)[v]_I−f,
and the corresponding ordinary-envelope identity. Thus q−f corresponds to obstacle −f; it need not be the new zero-obstacle envelope. No smallness assumption on f or modification mass law is needed.

Supporting-proof and source checks. Foundations 0–4 are applied only to genuine local representatives and closed positive auxiliary currents. The excluded Siu scan locator is not positive evidence; the applicable subtraction and countable-limit argument is Demailly III.8.15–8.16. Its trace polarization must use the degree-correct power p for bidimension (p,p); an inconsistent exponent in the intermediate display is a degree typo. Foundations 5–6 are used with the exact common closed background and Bergman parameter described above. Foundations 7–8 apply to bounded local potentials or finite closed products on Kähler manifolds. The multilinearity proof omitted from the printed BEGZ proposition is reconstructed by bounded multilinearity on intersections of strict finite superlevels and exhaustion; omitted pole sets are pluripolar.

For foundations 9 and 13, the auxiliary product construction in Witt Nyström compares cohomologous closed positive currents with small unbounded locus on P²×P^N. Those hypotheses hold there, without being imposed on the original arbitrary countable profile. In its quadratic Legendre calculation the vertical Hessian is 2Σdx_i∧d^c x_i. Using the actual fiber Monge–Ampère measure absorbs this vertical factor. Ordinary exterior powers also require binomial(n+N,N) in the product pushforward. Retain this common positive coefficient on BOTH comparison sides; it cancels. Bounded decreasing approximation and plurifine exhaustion establish the corrected moment comparison. Closed multilinearity makes the mixed mass a finite continuous polynomial, while N t^(N−1) concentrates at t=1. This proves the needed application. The local truncation notation should be v_C=max(v,u−C). The erroneous unconverted source formulas are not premises.

Foundation 10 is used only for bounded corrected products, their positivity and consistent restriction; the necessary unbounded limit was proved above. Foundations 11–12 undergo the actual-ideal and weight conversion already detailed. Foundation 14 is used solely in a fixed closed positive background with smooth probability measure and the ψ/2 operator conversion. Foundation 15 is used solely for locally corrected psh logarithms on a fixed modification, after establishing L¹ boundedness.

Foundation 16 also validates the ancillary bounded-mass-invariance proof. For a bounded potential, decreasing analytic approximants stay above that bound, hence have no analytic poles and are smooth in the source’s smooth-remainder convention. Subtract one common upper bound and divide the resulting nonpositive approximants by 1+dε_j, choosing dω>ω_X. The scaled sequence remains decreasing, is smoothly strictly ω-psh, and tends to the bounded potential up to a constant. Bounded product continuity then applies. If the coefficient 2 is used with only θ≥κ/2, it guarantees nonnegative admissibility; strict admissibility requires a larger coefficient. This is a harmless constant clarification. The supplied polarization proof detects dd^c(ω^j), and the power identities give the stated differential conditions. Its bounded extension is established using the permitted foundations, rather than imported as an extra [Chiose theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05945).

The supplied global-potential patching argument is valid: local potential differences are smooth, a partition of unity produces a global distribution and smooth closed residual, and local elliptic regularity gives uniqueness modulo smooth functions. The known countable domination proof follows by finite closed subtraction, passage to the countable limit and canonical recovery. The historical finite-divisor companion has unexpanded rigidity dependencies; only its elementary divisor-removal step is checked here, and its rigidity conclusion is not used by A–F.

The original review’s fourteen foundations and nineteen short bindings were compared with the applicable primary contexts. Their locator fragments and earlier PASS were not substituted for full hypotheses or applications. The current author’s disclosed inclusion of u in the Choquet maxima now supplies domination explicitly; the convention/citation clarification correctly identifies stabilized BFJ ideals and excludes the unconverted Darvas–Xia formula. No substantial repair of A–F is needed.

Finally, n5’s extra assertions for the constructed u are established. The obstacle argument proves ordinary/ideal equality at zero and every smooth obstacle. Ordinary equivalence and D give equality of upper volumes. For the original stretching definition choose C≥0 with q≤u+C and set a_t=u−(t−1)C. Then t⁻¹a_t+(1−t⁻¹)q≤u; treat t=1 as the endpoint a₁=u and interpret common poles canonically. This proves membership in E_env without replacing its definition by envelope equality. These conclusions are not extended to every v in the ideal class.

The exact contribution is a sufficient family specified by actual birational ideal-order limits, a summable hyperplane profile and an explicit positive pluriclosed residual, with an exact mass for every ordinary-type representative. Its example has infinite nonanalytic support and no single hyperplane pencil. Known countable envelope equivalence and bounded pluriclosed mass invariance retain their credit. No logical independence from every unspecified broader curve or fibration criterion, priority claim, or whole-original completion follows. The already established failure of (ii)→(i) at zero lower ideal volume is neither reopened nor repackaged.
